name: Nesmith Hall
use: UNH Sustainability Institute (relocating); historically Agricultural Experiment Station and plant/animal sciences
architect: Original based on a design by William Butterfield; 1932 and 1938–39 work by Eric T. Huddleston
style: Colonial Revival (originally Gothic Revival with a tower)
statusNote: Phase 1 closure list, Oct 2025; Sustainability Institute relocating

renovations.what: Remodeled from Gothic Revival to Colonial Revival and raised to three floors (Huddleston)
Two ninety-foot wings added, quadrupling the building
Significant interior renovation during the 1960s (exact year unknown)

facts.text: One of the first buildings after the 1893 move from Hanover, built for the Agricultural Experiment Station and named for Judge George W. Nesmith.
Its original design was noted as eccentric; the student paper called it 'pig-faced' in 1929.
Labs moved out after Rudman Hall opened (1996), and it served for a time as swing space during the Dimond and Pettee renovations.
Its occupants describe it as one of the least sustainable, least energy-efficient buildings on campus.

verdict: 1893 experiment-station building, remodelled to Colonial Revival in 1932; its tenants call it among the least efficient on campus, and it is slated for closure.
notes: The 1965 date is a placeholder for 'significant interior renovation during the 1960s' (archives); the exact year is unknown. Clio (2024) says it is now the plant and animal science headquarters with classrooms only; TNH (Dec 2025) says it houses the Sustainability Institute. Treat Clio's current-use line as stale. Closure execution unconfirmed. No licensed modern photo; ref-01 (archives) shows the long Colonial Revival front on Main Street; ref-02 (Clio) shows its three stages.
judgeNotes: Archives photo shows a decent porticoed brick front; only a 1909 licensed image survives.
